subject: POC shakedown: acceptance calendar & MAP for environment commissioning
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Megan Ruiz <megan@cardiologix.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: POC shakedown: acceptance calendar & MAP for environment commissioning

Hi Megan —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our conversation, attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (Draft_MAP_CardioLogix.pdf) that outlines the acceptance calendar and the minimal gating for the POC environment. High-level items we captured:

- Org creation and service account provisioning (Redwood org seeded w/ tenant ID)
- API keys issuance and scoped test tokens
- IP allowlist entries for CardioLogix staging CIDR ranges
- VPC peering and routing validation (optional: transit VPC for multi-region)
- Acceptance criteria: successful inference flow on a production-like sample (50k tokens/day throughput target), latency under 120ms p95 for 1-worker tests

Proposed acceptance calendar (flexible):
- Week 0 (May 3–7): Org & API keys issued, initial auth smoke tests
- Week 1 (May 10–14): IP allowlist & basic ingestion; API-level workload test
- Week 2 (May 17–21): VPC peering established and E2E validation
- Week 3 (May 24–28): Performance burn-in and signoff

If you prefer compressing the peering step we can run the peering + E2E on the same week but we recommend a 48–72 hour soak after peering to catch connection/route flapping.

Can you confirm the infra contact who will own peering and whether CardioLogix will complete a pre-provisioning checklist (CIDR blocks, firewall owner, contact)? I included Ben and Neha here for scheduling and runbook alignment — they’ll own the Redwood-side tasks and the acceptance runbook.

I attached a stub runbook (poc-acceptance-runbook.txt) and the MAP. Walk-through call available next Tue or Wed — suggest May 4 at 10 AM PT if that works.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Draft_MAP_CardioLogix.pdf (application/pdf), poc-acceptance-runbook.txt (text/plain)

From: Megan Ruiz <megan@cardiologix.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: infrastructure@cardiologix.com
Date: 2027-04-25T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC shakedown: acceptance calendar & MAP for environment commissioning

Sean —

Appreciate the walkthrough and the MAP draft. High level looks good. A couple of quick items from our side:

1) Our infra lead (infra@cardiologix.com) is looped — they asked if we can move the VPC peering to the week of May 10 rather than May 17 to align with a maintenance window we have scheduled on May 18. That would compress Week 1 and Week 2.
2) For the IP allowlist, we will provide both staging and failover CIDR blocks; expected time to update ACLs is same day but we need the list by EOD May 5.
3) We’d like a brief decision tree in the MAP: fallback to hosted endpoint if peering delays >72h.

We can do the May 4 walk-through at 10 AM PT. I’ll have infra on the call to confirm peering windows.

— Megan
VP Product, CardioLogix

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Megan Ruiz <megan@cardiologix.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T19:15:00-07:00
Subject: RE: POC shakedown: acceptance calendar & MAP for environment commissioning

Folks —

Thanks for the heads-up, Megan. Quick internal alignment on Redwood priorities and owners:

- Sean: external owner / MAP shepherd / exec touchpoints
- Ben: networking & peering lead (will own BGP/session validation and route propagation)
- Neha (me): acceptance runbook + test harness, performance burn-in owner
- Marissa: CS handoff and contractual close cadence (will coordinate any credit/discount asks)

Operational notes / adjustments:
- We can move VPC peering forward to May 10–12 but we recommend keeping May 17–21 as the burn-in window if CardioLogix intends to run a heavy production-like load; otherwise the soak will be short. Ben, please confirm whether a two-day peering + validation window is sufficient.
- For the IP allowlist requirement, capture: staging CIDR, failover CIDR, NAT gateway egress ranges, and the firewall owner contact. We will create a HubSpot ticket and attach the runbook checklist. HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/120-51923 (DL-2027-01923).
- We will include a short rollback plan in the MAP: fall back to Redwood-hosted endpoint (no peering) with a DNS TTL-based switch and scoped API keys. That gives CardioLogix continuity while peering is resolved.

Action items:
1) Sean: run through updated MAP on Tue May 4, include infra contact.
2) Megan/infra: provide CIDRs + firewall contact by EOD May 5.
3) Ben: confirm peering window and preflight checklist by Apr 28.
4) Neha: publish acceptance runbook on the HubSpot deal and share link before the May 4 call.

I’ll draft the short decision-tree language for the fallback and attach to the MAP.

-Neha
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-04-26T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC shakedown: acceptance calendar & MAP for environment commissioning

Megan —

Great — confirmed for the May 4 walkthrough at 10 AM PT. Ben flagged that May 10–12 is workable for peering provided we get the CIDRs by May 5 (we’ll start the BGP session prep immediately). We’ve updated the MAP to reflect the compressed peering window and added the fallback decision tree: if peering is not green within 72 hours, CardioLogix may switch to hosted endpoint while we resolve routing; Redwood will provide a scoped short-lived API key for continuity.

Next steps:
- Megan / infra: CIDRs + firewall contact by EOD May 5
- Ben: peering preflight checklist (Apr 28) — Ben will post notes to the HubSpot deal
- Neha: publish the acceptance runbook (expected Apr 27) to the HubSpot deal and share the link (also attached here).

DocuSign: if you’re comfortable with the MAP as a binding checklist for the POC gates, I’ll send a short DocuSign for signature after the May 4 call (covers mutual commitments and close timeline).

See you Tue — thanks everyone.

Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
